<b>Kostnad och hastighet.</b> Varje outp: Cost and speed. Every output token is a forward pass. More tokens per word means slower answers.
<b>Kontextfönstret</b> mäts i tokens, in: The context window is measured in tokens, not words.
<b>Konstiga fel.</b> Modellen ser aldrig: Strange failures. The model never sees the individual letters in “atten”, which is why counting letters is hard for it.
<b>Tokenizern måste matcha modellen.</b>: The tokenizer has to match the model. The wrong tokenizer gives ids that point at the wrong rows in the embedding table.
Mellanslag hör oftast till början av näs: A space usually belongs to the start of the next token. Swedish is split into more pieces than English because the tokenizer was trained mostly on English.

Tecken för tecken ger korta vokabulärer: Character by character gives small vocabularies but very long sequences, and attention costs more the longer the sequence gets.
Hela ord ger korta sekvenser men en enor: Whole words give short sequences but an enormous vocabulary and no way to handle new words.
Subword-tokens (BPE) är en kompromiss: v: Subword tokens (BPE) are a compromise: common words become a single token, rare ones are split up.
Computers work with numbers, not letters. So the text is first chopped into pieces, tokens, and each piece gets a number.
Modellen räknar bara med tal. Texten mås: The model only computes with numbers. The text has to be split into pieces that each carry an id in a fixed vocabulary.
<b>Byte Pair Encoding</b> tränas en gång: Byte Pair Encoding is trained once, before the model is trained: start from single bytes, find the most common pair in the training text, merge it into a new token, and repeat until the vocabulary is full. Llama 3 has 128,256 tokens.
